tm.details: The stream tests fail both hidden empty-body cases (upload and download completion events absent). Chromium tests passed, but Firefox/WebKit executables are unavailable.

opencode.details: The hidden stream tests passed, including empty response completion; Chromium empty-response browser test passed. Overall command failed because Firefox/WebKit executables are unavailable.

arms.better: tm indexed the repository quickly and went directly to source/utils/body.ts, but the provider returned a 429 before any plan or code change could be made. The terminal error said to retry, while tm events recorded ticket.retry_scheduled and the final stats reported only 1 second of wall time despite the command taking 13.56 seconds. Make the run summary reconcile observed wall time with event-derived stats, explicitly show the scheduled retry and the exact next command, and provide a direct resume/retry action so a transient provider limit does not leave the user to infer whether work will continue.

OpenCode stated a scoped plan, found the flush guard, implemented the completion callback with an empty Uint8Array, added regression coverage, and accurately surfaced that the full npm test command is blocked by a pre-existing lint error while the stream tests pass. It also investigated the unrelated pnpm build-approval files created during install; this consumed some extra context. The hidden stream tests passed. The browser suite could only run Chromium because Firefox/WebKit binaries were unavailable; preinstalling the browser engines would allow complete verification.
